title: Define selective pinning policy and metadata schema for ingesting nonstandard open-model variants
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: We routinely ingest community/open model variants that deviate from our canonical runtime expectations (e.g., nonstandard KV cache layout, mixed-precision weights, or nonstandard tokenizer metadata). Historically we've defaulted to either full pinning (block until validated) or coarse acceptance with manual follow-up. This binary approach is slowing intake and producing noisy rollback churn.

Objective: Define a selective pinning policy and a machine-readable intake metadata schema that lets engineers admit useful experimental variants to the catalog with constrained runtime risk, clear metadata-driven compatibility assertions, and automated telemetry guards. This ticket clarifies requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout steps for the PM/Eng/Design work needed to implement the policy.

Scope:
- Define required and optional metadata fields submitted with any open-model intake (compat_level, pin_strategy, kernel_compat_tags, tokenizer_hash, kv_layout_hint, expected_max_token_len, fallback_variant).
- Define three pin_strategy values: "auto-allow-with-guardrails", "soft-pin", "hard-pin" and their operational semantics.
- Map metadata to runtime admission checks and routing behavior (canary traffic fraction, telemetry tags, automated fallback triggers).
- Define telemetry events and SLO thresholds that trigger automated pin escalation or rollback.
- Create an intake UI/CLI contract and PRD appendix for Solutions/Support to use.

Out of scope: Full implementation of runtime automatic rollback hooks (will be follow-up ENG tickets).

Stakeholders: Product (Asha P.), Runtime Eng (Ravi Kumar), Catalog Eng (Priya Singh), Security/Compliance (Marta Ruiz), Developer Experience (Evan Chen), Design (Nora Park).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Ambiguous metadata leads to inconsistent acceptance. Mitigation: Provide strict validation schema and examples, require critical fields for any nonstandard variant.
- Risk: Too-liberal auto-allow could increase incidents. Mitigation: Default auto-allow to low-traffic canary routing with telemetry gating.

Deliverables:
1) Metadata schema document (JSON Schema + human-friendly reference)
2) Pin strategy definition doc with runtime semantics and escalation matrix
3) Intake UI/CLI spec for required fields and error states
4) Telemetry spec and SLO guard thresholds to attach to catalog entries
5) Acceptance tests and evaluation checklist for intake reviewers

Reference artifacts: Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Catalog/Selective+Pinning+PRD (draft), GitHub PR blueprint: https://github.com/redwood-inference/catalog/pulls (template), runtime telemetry dashboard mock: https://dash.redwood.ai/model-catalog/ingest-canary (prototype)
acceptance_criteria: A JSON Schema file exists and validates ingestion payloads; required fields: compat_level, pin_strategy, tokenizer_hash, expected_max_token_len
Pin strategy semantics documented: 'auto-allow-with-guardrails', 'soft-pin', 'hard-pin' with routing and traffic fraction examples
Catalogue ingestion API returns explicit advisories when a submitted model requires 'hard-pin' and blocks non-admin admission
Runtime must accept metadata and route canary traffic per pin_strategy: default 1% for auto-allow, configurable for soft-pin
Telemetry spec lists events (ingest_received, canary_latency, canary_error_rate, fallback_triggered) and SLO thresholds that cause automated escalation to hard-pin
Reviewer checklist exists with pass/fail items and example inputs; at least two catalog engineers have signed off
UX/CLI mockups for intake are reviewed by Design and Developer Experience and linked in the PRD
A documented rollback/escalation playbook is attached with clear owner and on-call contact
Unit/e2e test vectors for three representative nonstandard variants (tokenizer mismatch, odd kv_layout, mixed-precision quant) included with expected results

2025-03-11 Priya Singh (Catalog): Suggest adding 'fallback_variant' metadata to indicate candidate compatible variant for automated routing on error; also explicit support window for soft-pin variants (default 14 days).
2025-03-12 Nora Park (Design): Will prepare intake form states for each pin_strategy and validation error messaging. Need examples for 'auto-allow-with-guardrails'.
2025-03-12 Marty Ruiz (Security): Security review requested for any model that requests 'auto-allow-with-guardrails' and has external provenance links. Marking for compliance triage.
2025-03-12 Liam O'Connor: Consolidating feedback, will schedule a cross-functional working session 2025-03-14 to finalize schema and routing semantics.
notes: This ticket captures policy and contract—not runtime enforcement code. After acceptance we'll spawn ENG work items for runtime admit checks, telemetry hooks, and automated fallback handlers. Ensure each spawned ENG ticket references PM-101010.
